items.text: The parent initiative's context doc (agent-sandbox-audit-foundation/context/2026-04-09-sandbox-audit-foundation.md) already locks several contract directions: tracking-first (not security-first), `manualReview=false`, `autoApply=true`, `applyOnFailure=true`, `lock=false`, lock and acceptance orthogonal, network modes `none|localhost|full`, agent-prompt-transparency. This research's job is to convert those directional decisions into a precise, named contract and reconcile current code against it — not to relitigate them. Decisions below focus on the open contract questions the initiative did NOT pre-decide.

Two acceptance_allow globs in spec.json point to non-existent paths in the current repo: `scripts/lib/scenario/**` and `cli/commands/scenario/**`. The initiative context references the same paths (e.g., `scripts/lib/scenario/runner.sh`, `cli/commands/scenario/modules/heal.sh`) but neither resolves on disk. Either the lifecycle scripts moved or the references are stale. Decision d6 below addresses this directly.

items.topic: Mode taxonomy in v1 of the contract
items.context: The initiative envisions two long-term modes (`tracking` and `protected`). The contract being authored now is the auditability-first contract. Question: does v1 of the contract introduce the explicit `mode` field with two named values now (so future protected-mode work has a slot to land in), or does it define only the tracking behavior and leave `mode` as an implicit constant until protected-mode work begins? Naming the field early costs little and prevents protected-mode work from having to retrofit; deferring keeps the immediate config surface smaller.

options.label: Introduce explicit `mode: tracking | protected` field now, with `tracking` default and `protected` reserved (errors if requested before implemented)
options.rationale: Forward-compatible; documents the long-term shape; protected-mode work can land without a config-surface migration

options.label: No explicit mode field in v1; the contract describes today's behavior as 'tracking-first' implicitly
options.rationale: Smaller surface area now; defers naming until protected mode is real

options.label: Other (specify)
options.rationale: Describe an alternative taxonomy

items.topic: Default network mode for sandboxed agent-manager runs
items.context: The initiative requires support for `none|localhost|full`. It also notes that scenario CLIs are thin wrappers over local scenario APIs, so `none` would break common agent workflows. What is the documented default for sandboxed agent-manager runs? `localhost` keeps scenario CLIs working out of the box; `full` matches today's de facto behavior with no breakage; `none` is most defensive but breaks scenario CLI usage by default.

options.label: `localhost` — agent can reach loopback APIs but not the open internet
options.rationale: Aligns with the explicit initiative note that scenario CLIs depend on localhost; tightens vs today without breaking workflows

options.label: `full` — preserve today's behavior
options.rationale: Zero-risk for existing flows; defers any tightening to protected mode

options.label: `none` — most defensive default
options.rationale: Strongest auditability story, but explicitly breaks scenario CLI usage per initiative note

options.label: Other (specify)
options.rationale: Different default or per-spawn-surface defaults

items.topic: Definition of 'apply' for failed runs that produced changes
items.context: `applyOnFailure=true` is the directional default. But what counts as 'failure' for this purpose, and is the apply behavior identical to a successful run, or attenuated? Options: apply identically regardless of outcome (simplest, matches spec); apply but mark provenance as `from_failed_run=true` so GCT can surface it differently; only apply on certain failure classes (e.g., agent error vs test failure vs infra error).

options.label: Identical apply behavior; record run outcome in provenance metadata so GCT can render differently
options.rationale: Simple, matches initiative intent, gives GCT a single hook to differentiate visually without contract complexity

options.label: Apply identically with no outcome metadata distinction
options.rationale: Smallest contract surface; loses ability to filter or warn on failed-run provenance

options.label: Apply only when failure is agent-side (e.g., crash, timeout); skip apply on infrastructure errors
options.rationale: Avoids applying changes from runs where infra issues might have corrupted state, but introduces failure-class taxonomy

options.label: Other (specify)
options.rationale: Different framing for failure handling

items.topic: Pending-vs-committed provenance lifecycle in Git Control Tower
items.context: The spec calls out that GCT already has pending provenance plumbing and an AI Changes tab, but the lifecycle for pending-vs-committed provenance is not formally defined. Pending = sandbox applied but no git commit yet; committed = git commit recorded. Question: does pending provenance auto-promote to committed when GCT detects a commit touching the same files, or only via an explicit operator action, or always pending until manually associated?

options.label: Auto-promote on commit detection: when a commit's changed files overlap a pending provenance record's files, GCT links them automatically
options.rationale: Lowest operator overhead; matches the auditability-first goal of effortless attribution

options.label: Operator-confirmed promotion: GCT proposes the link, operator confirms in the AI Changes tab
options.rationale: Higher confidence in correctness; adds friction

options.label: Always pending until explicit association via API/CLI
options.rationale: Keeps pending and committed strictly separate; relies on commit-time tooling to associate

options.label: Other (specify)
options.rationale: Alternative lifecycle

items.topic: Behavior when changes exist outside `acceptanceAllow` at end of run
items.context: Initiative says 'changes outside acceptance can exist in the sandbox during execution but should not auto-apply.' Open question: at run end, how are out-of-acceptance changes surfaced? Options: (A) silently retained in sandbox, available for inspection but never applied; (B) surfaced as a warning + GCT review queue entry the operator can approve manually; (C) auto-discarded at run end; (D) blocking — run fails closed if any out-of-acceptance change exists.

options.label: Retain silently in sandbox; only in-acceptance changes auto-apply; operator can inspect via GCT
options.rationale: Matches 'transparent to agent' principle and 'auditability-first'; preserves all evidence without breaking runs

options.label: Retain + surface as a GCT review-queue entry the operator can manually approve to apply
options.rationale: Best operator experience: nothing is lost, useful out-of-scope work is recoverable, default still safe

options.label: Auto-discard out-of-acceptance changes at run end
options.rationale: Simplest end-state but destroys evidence and contradicts auditability-first framing

options.label: Fail the run if any change is out of acceptance
options.rationale: Strongest enforcement but breaks the 'agent transparent to sandbox' principle since the agent has no way to know acceptance

options.label: Other (specify)
options.rationale: Different end-state policy

items.context: Both globs point to paths that don't exist in the repo. The initiative context references files in those paths (e.g., `scripts/lib/scenario/runner.sh`). Either the scenario-restart and lifecycle scripts moved/were renamed, or the references are pre-refactor. Since this item is research and writes to `conclusion.md` (in the backlog item folder, not the repo), the acceptance_allow only matters for documentation actions the conclusion may propose. Question: how should the contract treat these references?

options.label: Locate the current scenario-restart/lifecycle code paths via repo search, replace the stale globs with the actual paths in `acceptance_allow`
options.rationale: Most accurate; ensures the source-of-truth matrix in Finding 3 references real files

options.label: Remove both globs from acceptance_allow; document in Limitations that the scenario-restart surface lookup is a known gap to resolve in a follow-on item
options.rationale: Lowest-effort; defers the discovery

options.label: Keep the globs as-is and add them to `creates`, treating them as paths the research recommends restoring
options.rationale: Only valid if the research will recommend creating those exact files, which is unlikely

options.label: Other (specify)
options.rationale: Different resolution

items.topic: Where the final contract document lives
items.context: The deliverable is `conclusion.md` inside this backlog item — that is non-negotiable per the research-conclusion authoring skill. But the contract also needs a discoverable home for downstream agents and humans (operators, contributors). Should the conclusion's actions also produce a copy/canonical doc somewhere in the repo, and if so where?

options.label: Mirror the contract into `scenarios/workspace-sandbox/docs/AUDITABILITY_CONTRACT.md` (closest to the implementation surface)
options.rationale: Co-located with the primary implementation; easy for workspace-sandbox contributors to find

options.label: Mirror into `scenarios/agent-manager/docs/SANDBOX_CONTRACT.md` (closest to the consumer surface)
options.rationale: Closer to the run-orchestration code that depends on the contract

options.label: Add a top-level `docs/contracts/sandbox-auditability.md`
options.rationale: Discoverable from the docs index; signals cross-scenario contract

options.label: Conclusion-only; no repo mirror in this research's scope
options.rationale: Keeps research output self-contained; downstream items can mirror if needed

options.label: Other (specify)
options.rationale: Different location or multiple mirrors

plan_updates: Created conclusion.md scaffold with Research Question, Methodology (sources to read, mismatch reconciliation approach), Limitations (stale path refs, protected-mode out of scope, undo/revert out of scope, empirical validation deferred). Findings sections are placeholders that will fill as decisions converge. Actions block is commented-out anticipated shape, consistent with the parent initiative's existing members.
